title: The Metaphysically Given
summary: Facts that are, as against facts that human choice brings into existence. What is given is not up for a vote.

lessons.title: Facts that are
lessons.objective: Name a metaphysically given fact as something that is, not something a person decided to create.

exercises.prompt: What is the metaphysically given?

choices.text: Facts that are, apart from human choice
Facts that become true when enough people agree
Facts that exist only because someone chose to make them
Facts that change whenever a person feels differently

feedback.note: The metaphysically given is the side of facts that simply are. Human choice did not bring them into existence.

exercises.prompt: Which item is a fact that is, rather than a product of choice?

choices.text: Fire burns
A club rule that meetings start at noon
A song someone wrote
The name a parent picks for a child

feedback.note: Fire burns whether or not anyone chose that it should. A rule, a song, and a name exist because someone chose them.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the kind of fact it is.

feedback.note: Hardness and wetness are given. A road is there because people chose to build it.

exercises.prompt: Finish the line for this side of the distinction.

parts.text: The metaphysically given is facts that

feedback.note: The short name for this side is facts that are. They are not waiting on a decision.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states what the metaphysically given is.

feedback.note: Leave the distractors out. The given is facts that are, not ballots or opinions.

exercises.prompt: A mountain stands where it stands. What kind of fact is that?

choices.text: A metaphysically given fact
A statute someone passed
A habit a town invented
A brand a company launched

feedback.note: The mountain is there as a fact of reality. No human choice brought the mountain into existence.

exercises.prompt: Match the phrase to what it points at.

pairs.right: What brings some facts into existence
A fact that needed a decision

feedback.note: Keep the two sides apart. The given is what is. The other side exists because someone chose.

exercises.prompt: Name the topic of this unit in the blank.

parts.text: This unit is about the metaphysically

feedback.note: The name is the metaphysically given: facts that are, as against facts that choice brings about.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order so the sentence names only the given side.

feedback.note: A given fact simply is. A decree belongs on the choice side, so it stays out of this sentence.

lessons.title: Brought into existence by choice
lessons.objective: Identify facts that exist because human choice brought them into existence.

exercises.prompt: Which fact did human choice bring into existence?

choices.text: A bridge across a river
The river the bridge crosses
The fact that water flows downhill
The fact that iron is a metal

feedback.note: People chose to build the bridge. The river, the flow, and the metal are facts that are.

exercises.prompt: A city passes a speed limit. What kind of fact is the speed limit?

choices.text: A fact human choice brought into existence
A metaphysically given fact
A fact of nature no one enacted
The identity of the road surface itself

feedback.note: The limit exists because people chose it. The road's physical nature is a different kind of fact.

exercises.prompt: Match each product of choice to what made it a fact.

feedback.note: Laws, tools, and customs are facts, but they are facts that choice brought into existence.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast from the unit summary.

parts.text: Some facts are. Other facts are what human

feedback.note: The second side of the distinction is human choice. Weather, gravity, and stone stay on the given side.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about the choice side.

feedback.note: Choice brings some facts into existence. It does not erase nature, so those distractors do not belong.

exercises.prompt: Which pair puts a chosen fact next to a given fact?

choices.text: A calendar date for a holiday, and the length of a day
A recipe, and the restaurant that serves it
That ice is cold, and that iron sinks in water
A dress code, and a school bell schedule

feedback.note: A holiday date is chosen. The length of a day is a fact that is. The other pairs sit entirely on one side.

exercises.prompt: Sort each item.

pairs.left: The street name on the sign

feedback.note: The house and the street name exist because people decided. The ground is metaphysically given.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two blanks with the two sides.

parts.text: A poem is a product of

feedback.note: Someone chooses to write a poem. That sound travels is a fact that is, so it is given.

exercises.prompt: If nobody had ever chosen to invent money, what would follow?

choices.text: Money would not be a fact, because choice never brought it into existence
Money would still be metaphysically given
Nature would also fail to exist
A later vote could make the past invention unnecessary

feedback.note: Money is a fact only because human choice brought it into existence. The given does not depend on that choice.

lessons.title: Not up for a vote
lessons.objective: See that a metaphysically given fact is not settled by a vote, a poll, or a majority.

exercises.prompt: What does this unit say about what is given?

choices.text: It is not up for a vote
A majority can revise it
A tie vote leaves it undecided
Each person may opt out of it

feedback.note: What is given is not up for a vote. Agreement does not decide whether a given fact is a fact.

exercises.prompt: A meeting votes that stones float. What happens to the fact?

choices.text: Stones still do not float. The vote does not rewrite the given.
Stones start to float because the vote passed.
Stones float inside the meeting room only.
Stones float until the next election.

feedback.note: A vote can create a rule. It cannot turn a metaphysically given fact into its opposite.

exercises.prompt: Match each action to what it can change.

pairs.left: A vote on a club rule
pairs.right: A fact that choice can bring about

pairs.left: A poll about whether fire burns
pairs.right: Only the tally, not the burning

feedback.note: Votes settle chosen arrangements. They do not settle facts that are.

exercises.prompt: Finish the unit's line about the given.

parts.text: What is given is not up for a

feedback.note: The line is literal: what is given is not up for a vote.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that refuses to put the given on a ballot.

feedback.note: A given fact is not a ballot item. Calling it optional would miss the point, so that word stays unused.

exercises.prompt: Everyone in a town agrees that winter is summer. Which statement is right?

choices.text: The season is still whatever it is. Agreement is not a vote that rewrites it.
Winter becomes summer because everyone agrees.
The season becomes half of each.
The season changes only for the people who agreed.

feedback.note: Unanimous agreement is still not a power over the metaphysically given. The fact remains what it is.

exercises.prompt: Match the claim to the correction.

pairs.left: We voted, so the fact changed
pairs.right: A vote does not change the given
A majority is not the given

feedback.note: Votes, majorities, and repeals belong to facts that choice brings into existence. They do not govern facts that are.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks.

parts.text: A law can be up for a
. A given fact cannot be up for a

feedback.note: The same word marks the contrast. Chosen rules can be voted. What is given cannot.

exercises.prompt: Which question treats a given fact as if it were up for a vote?

choices.text: Shall we decide that heavy things fall upward?
Shall we build a bridge here?
Shall we change the meeting time?
Shall we name the new street?

feedback.note: Building, scheduling, and naming are matters of choice. Whether heavy things fall is a fact that is, so it is not a ballot question.

lessons.title: A wish is not the given
lessons.objective: Separate wanting a fact to be otherwise from the metaphysically given fact itself.

exercises.prompt: You wish a desert were a lake. What is true of the desert?

choices.text: It remains a desert. The wish does not replace the given fact.
It becomes a lake because you wish it.
It becomes a lake for you and a desert for others.
It waits until a vote confirms the wish.

feedback.note: A wish is not a way to bring a new nature into existence. The given fact stays what it is.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence respects the metaphysically given?

choices.text: The fact is what it is, whether or not I want it.
If I want it otherwise, the fact changes.
If we all want it otherwise, the fact changes.
If I ignore it, it stops being a fact.

feedback.note: Wanting, group wanting, and ignoring are not powers over facts that are.

exercises.prompt: Match each stance to the side it treats correctly.

pairs.left: I wish the rock were soft
pairs.right: A wish, not a change in the given

pairs.left: I choose to carve the rock
pairs.right: Choice acting on a given fact

feedback.note: You can choose what to do with a rock. You cannot wish the rock's nature out of existence.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

feedback.note: Wishing does not install a new fact in place of the metaphysically given.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that keeps the wish and the fact apart.

feedback.note: Wanting otherwise does not change what is given. The extra words would say something this lesson does not claim.

exercises.prompt: Someone dislikes that people need food. What follows?

choices.text: The need remains a given fact. Dislike is not a repeal.
The need ends because it is unwelcome.
The need was brought into existence by a vote.
Each person may decline the fact.

feedback.note: Dislike does not move a fact from the given side onto the choice side. The fact still is.

exercises.prompt: Match the mistake to what it confuses.

pairs.left: Treating a wish as a fact

pairs.right: Confuses a ballot with the given

pairs.left: Treating a tool as uncaused by people
pairs.right: Confuses a product of choice with a fact that is

feedback.note: Each mistake slides one side of the distinction over the other. Wishes and votes do not rewrite facts that are, and tools are not given.

exercises.prompt: Fill the blanks from the two sides.

parts.text: . The decision to carry an umbrella is

feedback.note: The storm is a fact that is. Carrying an umbrella is something a person chooses in light of that fact.

exercises.prompt: Order the words so the sentence states the limit on a wish.

feedback.note: A wish leaves the given fact unchanged. It does not rewrite reality.

lessons.title: Hold both sides
lessons.objective: Sort mixed cases by keeping facts that are on one side and facts that choice brings into existence on the other.

exercises.prompt: A farmer plants wheat in soil. Which split is right?

choices.text: Planting is choice. That seeds grow in soil is given.
Planting and the growth of seeds are both products of a vote.
The decision to plant is as given as the soil.
Neither planting nor growth is a fact.

feedback.note: Hold both sides at once. Choice brings the planting into existence. The way seeds grow is a fact that is.

exercises.prompt: Sort the mixed case of a ship at sea.

pairs.left: That wood floats or sinks as it does

feedback.note: People make the ship and pick the course. The sea and the way materials behave are given.

exercises.prompt: Which statement keeps the whole distinction?

choices.text: Facts that are stand apart from facts that human choice brings into existence, and the given is not up for a vote.
Every fact exists only because someone chose it.
Human choice never brings any fact into existence.
Both sides are up for a vote.

feedback.note: The unit needs both sides and the limit on voting. Dropping either side, or putting the given on a ballot, loses the distinction.

exercises.prompt: Fill the summary in order.

parts.text: , as against facts that human choice brings into existence. What is given is not up for a

feedback.note: Those two words carry the unit: facts that are, and not up for a vote.

exercises.prompt: Build one sentence that names both sides.

feedback.note: Some facts are, and some are chosen. None of the given facts are voted into being.

exercises.prompt: A language has a word for snow, and snow is cold. How do you sort them?

choices.text: The word is a product of choice. That snow is cold is given.
Both the word and the cold are products of choice.
Both the word and the cold are metaphysically given.
The cold is chosen and the word is given.

feedback.note: People bring words into existence by choice. The cold of snow is a fact that is, and no vocabulary vote changes it.

exercises.prompt: Match each test question to the answer it calls for.

pairs.left: Did human choice bring this into existence?
pairs.right: If yes, it is not the given

pairs.left: Would it still be a fact with no vote?

feedback.note: Use the unit's own tests. Choice accounts for one side. The other side is what is, and it is not up for a wish or a vote.

exercises.prompt: Label the two items.

parts.text: A courtroom is a product of

feedback.note: Courts exist because people chose to make them. Mortality is a fact that is, and it is not up for a vote.

exercises.prompt: After this unit, which error is still an error?

choices.text: Treating a given fact as something a vote or a wish can replace
Noticing that a bridge exists because people chose to build it
Noticing that fire burns whether or not anyone prefers that
Keeping the given and the chosen on different sides

feedback.note: The error is putting the metaphysically given up for a vote or a wish. The other three answers are the distinction held correctly.

exercises.prompt: Close the unit with the sentence in order.

feedback.note: What is given is not up for a vote. A wish does not take the place of that limit.
